answer: Slashable accuracy bonds. For pigment assays, zenith measurements, or relic inventories, lock a separate bond for each outstanding claim until its audit window closes. A verifier randomly audits evidence against a published objective test and forfeits the bond on proven fabrication. N simultaneous claims require N locked bonds, imposing capital or borrowing costs across aliases. Deterrence requires the expected forfeiture to exceed the gain from fraud; weak audits or undersized bonds let wealthy attackers profit.
